one_liner: Enterprise CRM platform with extensive multi-cloud APIs and customizable object metadata.
auth_notes: OAuth2 via Connected App or External Client App; JWT bearer flow for server-to-server; access token in Authorization header.
credential_path: Sign up for free Developer Edition org, create Connected/External Client App in Setup, enable OAuth scopes, copy client id/secret.
breadth_note: REST, SOAP, Bulk, Metadata and GraphQL APIs across hundreds of standard plus custom sObjects.

mcp.note: Salesforce-hosted MCP servers documented as GA for Enterprise Edition and above; salesforcecli/mcp also exists for dev tooling.

rate_limits: Daily org API request limits by edition/licenses; concurrent request caps.
notes: Free Developer Edition has API on. Customer Group/Professional orgs need a paid API add-on. AppExchange listing requires ISV security review.

one_liner: Inbound marketing, sales and service CRM with broad public REST APIs.
auth_notes: Private app access token (bearer) for single-account use; OAuth2 for multi-account or marketplace apps. Legacy static API keys retired.
credential_path: Create free HubSpot account, Settings > Integrations > Private Apps, pick scopes, copy token; or register developer app for OAuth.
breadth_note: CRM objects, marketing, CMS, conversations, automation; hundreds of endpoints plus associations and custom objects.

mcp.note: Two official servers: remote CRM MCP at mcp.hubspot.com (OAuth) and a local developer MCP for app/CMS building.

rate_limits: 100 req/10s for OAuth apps, 500 req/10s for private apps; daily caps.
notes: Listing a public app on the HubSpot App Marketplace requires app review; private/OAuth apps for own use do not. Some objects need paid tiers.

one_liner: Sales-pipeline-focused CRM with a mature versioned REST API.
auth_notes: Personal API token for own-account scripts; OAuth2 client id/secret from Developer Hub with scoped consent for multi-tenant apps.
credential_path: Start free trial, Personal preferences > API to copy token; or register an app in Pipedrive Developer Hub for OAuth credentials.
breadth_note: v1 and v2 REST across deals, persons, organizations, activities, products; published OpenAPI 3 specs and SDKs.

mcp.note: Native Pipedrive-built MCP server launched June 2026, reported available on all Pipedrive plans.

rate_limits: Token-budget per 2-second window; 10,000 POST/PUT per user daily.
notes: API access reported on every plan, but there is no permanent free tier so a trial or paid seat is needed. Marketplace listing needs Pipedrive review.

one_liner: Modern flexible-data-model CRM with a clean, well-documented REST API.
auth_notes: Workspace API key used as Bearer token, or per-user OAuth2 authorization-code access token; both use the same Bearer scheme.
credential_path: Create Attio workspace, Workspace Settings > Developers, create an integration and API key with scopes; OAuth app for distribution.
breadth_note: REST over objects, records, lists, entries, notes, tasks, comments and webhooks; attribute schema is workspace-defined.

mcp.note: Official remote MCP with OAuth login and dynamic client registration; docs at docs.attio.com/mcp/overview. Some SQL tools are plan-gated.

rate_limits: 100 read req/s, 25 write req/s; 429 with Retry-After header.
notes: One third-party blog claimed API access needs approval and 1,000 calls/hour; official docs show self-serve keys, so that claim is treated as unreliable.

one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable CRM with auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs.
auth_notes: Workspace API key sent as Bearer token; created in Settings > API & Webhooks and optionally scoped to a role.
credential_path: Self-host from GitHub or sign up for Twenty Cloud, then Settings > API & Webhooks > Create key and copy it once.
breadth_note: Core CRUD at /rest and /graphql plus metadata API at /rest/metadata; endpoints follow each workspace's own schema.

mcp.note: Several community MCP servers exist; an official one was still an open feature request (twentyhq/twenty issue 12953). Some blogs claim a native Cloud MCP — unverified.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: Schema is per-workspace with no static API reference, so the tool surface must be generated at runtime.
notes: Unconfirmed: official MCP status and rate limits. Self-hosted instances have no vendor-enforced limits; Cloud limits not found in docs.

one_liner: Progress-owned low-code work and CRM platform built on configurable apps.
auth_notes: OAuth2 only against api.podio.com: server-side flow, app authentication (app id + app token), or username/password flow.
credential_path: Create Podio account, register an API client in account settings to get client_id and client_secret, then run an OAuth flow.
breadth_note: Large REST surface: items, apps, orgs, spaces, tasks, files, comments, hooks, views and more.

mcp.note: Official Podio MCP server documented at mcp.podio.com in Progress/ShareFile docs; read and write over workspaces, apps and items.

rate_limits: Hourly per-client limit; third-party cites 250/hour, not verified officially.
notes: Unconfirmed: exact rate-limit numbers. Product moved from Citrix to Progress Software and is actively maintained, not sunset.

one_liner: Zoho suite CRM with a v8 REST API and credit-based rate limiting.
auth_notes: OAuth2 only; Self Client grant for server-to-server, authorization code for user apps. Access tokens last one hour, refresh tokens persist.
credential_path: Register a client (Self Client or Server-based) in Zoho API Console, pick scopes, generate auth code, exchange for refresh token.
breadth_note: Records, modules, COQL queries, bulk read/write, metadata, notifications; datacenter-specific domains (.com/.eu/.in).

mcp.note: Zoho runs mcp.zoho.com with prebuilt CRM servers (Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, Workflow Automation). Exact doc URL unverified.

rate_limits: Credit-based daily limits by edition (Free 5,000/day); concurrency 5-25 calls.
notes: Free edition confirmed to have API credits. Multi-datacenter token/domain handling adds integration complexity. Zoho MCP docs URL not directly retrieved.

one_liner: Inside-sales CRM with built-in calling, email and a REST API.
auth_notes: API key sent via HTTP Basic (key as username, empty password); OAuth2 client id/secret yields a Bearer access token.
credential_path: Start a Close trial, Settings > API Keys > generate key; or register an OAuth app in Close developer settings for client id/secret.
breadth_note: Leads, contacts, opportunities, activities (calls, emails, SMS), custom fields, smart views, reporting.

mcp.note: Official remote MCP at mcp.close.com/mcp with streamable HTTP and OAuth2 dynamic client registration.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint-group limits via RateLimit headers; org limit 3x key limit.
notes: Close publishes no fixed numeric rate limit; limits are per endpoint group and exposed in headers. No free plan, so trial or paid seat needed.

one_liner: Google Workspace-native CRM with a header-key REST API.
auth_notes: API key via X-PW-AccessToken plus X-PW-UserEmail headers. OAuth2 client credentials are only issued after contacting partners@copper.com.
credential_path: For keys: System Settings > API Keys > Generate API Key in the Copper app. For OAuth: email partners@copper.com to register an app.
breadth_note: REST v1 for people, companies, opportunities, leads, tasks, activities, projects and webhook subscriptions.

mcp.note: No official Copper MCP found; several community and aggregator-hosted servers (Apideck, Pipedream, n8n, viaSocket) exist.

rate_limits: Third-party sources cite ~600 req/min per key; official figure unconfirmed.
blocker: OAuth client credentials require Copper partner approval; only per-user API keys are self-serve.
notes: OAuth explicitly requires registering with Copper's partner team, so multi-tenant toolkits need outreach; API-key-only single-tenant builds work today.

one_liner: Intapp's deal and relationship CRM for private capital and advisory firms.
auth_notes: OAuth2 client-credentials bearer token; the client id/secret come from an API key generated in the user profile after admin enablement.
credential_path: Admin enables API under Admin > User Management > Capabilities > Site Areas, then user Profile > API Key > Enable and copy.
breadth_note: Data, schema, user management, RelIntel, publications and eMarketing endpoints over a tenant-configured schema.

mcp.note: DealCloud MCP server documented, reported as client preview from July 2026; responses scoped to requesting user's permissions.

rate_limits: 5 req/s data, schema, user mgmt; 300/min auth; 1000/s eMarketing.
blocker: Requires a licensed DealCloud tenant plus admin-granted API capability; no public sandbox or self-signup found.
notes: Docs are public but credentials are gated behind a paid tenant and an admin. Webhook/event-notification support not confirmed in retrieved docs.

one_liner: Enterprise ticketing and omnichannel customer service suite with a large marketplace.
auth_notes: OAuth2 bearer is recommended; API tokens use Basic as email/token:token and are scheduled for deactivation on 30 April 2027.
credential_path: Sign up for a trial, then Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > Zendesk API to create a token or OAuth client.
breadth_note: Tickets, users, orgs, Help Center, Talk, Chat, views, triggers, macros, custom objects, Sunshine.

mcp.note: Zendesk officially ships an MCP client for action flows. Several blogs claim a first-party per-tenant MCP server at <subdomain>.zendesk.com/api/mcp, but other sources deny it and I found no official Zendesk doc confirming it.

rate_limits: 200-700 req/min by plan; 2500 with High Volume API add-on
blocker: Multi-tenant distribution needs a global OAuth client granted by Zendesk; API tokens deactivate April 2027.
notes: Apps distributed via the Zendesk Marketplace go through app review; global OAuth clients require a Zendesk request. MCP server status unconfirmed.

one_liner: Messenger-first support platform with Fin AI agent, inbox, and help center.
auth_notes: Access token issued instantly when you create an app in Developer Hub; OAuth2 for public apps, no refresh tokens.
credential_path: Create a free development workspace, create an app in Developer Hub, copy the token from Configure > Authentication, or enable OAuth.
breadth_note: Conversations, contacts, companies, tickets, articles, events, data attributes, tags, admins, notes.

mcp.note: First-party hosted server (EU at mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp, AU unsupported), OAuth2 or bearer token, ~14 tools across conversations, contacts, companies, and articles.

rate_limits: ~10,000 calls/min per private app; 25,000/min per workspace
notes: Private apps need no review but require a paid workspace; public App Store apps require Intercom review and App Partner Program pages.

one_liner: Freshworks cloud helpdesk with ticketing, automations, and a free starter tier.
auth_notes: v2 REST API uses HTTP Basic with the API key as username and any string as password; no OAuth2 on v2.
credential_path: Sign up (free tier available), open your agent profile settings, and copy the API key shown on the profile page.
breadth_note: Tickets, conversations, contacts, companies, agents, groups, solutions/KB, surveys, time entries, products.

mcp.note: Freshworks MCP integration reported generally available from 10 September 2026; authenticates via API key only. Multiple community servers also exist (e.g. NeuraLegion/freshdesk_mcp).

rate_limits: 100-700 req/min per account by plan; 429 with Retry-After
notes: Webhooks are fired from automation/observer rules rather than a first-class subscription API, and cover ticket events more than contact/agent lifecycle.

one_liner: Shared inbox and customer operations platform built around team email collaboration.
auth_notes: API tokens sent as Bearer; OAuth2 required for public integrations on the App Store unless Front grants an exception.
credential_path: Company settings > Developers > API tokens to create a token; or register an OAuth app in the developer portal for public apps.
breadth_note: Conversations, messages, comments, drafts, contacts, accounts, inboxes, teammates, tags, rules, analytics.

mcp.note: Front's hosted MCP server at mcp.frontapp.com/mcp (open beta since mid-2026), OAuth-authenticated, ~18 tools over conversations, messages, tags, and contacts.

rate_limits: 50/100/200 req/min by plan; 120 rpm for partner OAuth apps
blocker: Multi-tenant/public integrations must use OAuth via Front's app framework unless Front grants a written exception.
notes: Front requires partner OAuth for anything acting on another company's Front account, so production multi-tenant use is effectively partner-gated.

one_liner: B2B support platform centered on Slack, Teams, and shared customer channels.
auth_notes: REST API uses Bearer token generated in the dashboard; the hosted MCP server uses OAuth 2.0 via AuthKit.
credential_path: Start a paid plan or trial, then go to app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens and generate an API token.
breadth_note: Issues, accounts, contacts, teams, users, custom fields, knowledge base, and webhook configuration.

mcp.note: Pylon hosts mcp.usepylon.com over Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.0; enabled from Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server; reads and updates issues, accounts, contacts.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Rate limits not found in public docs. Pricing appears self-serve from ~$59/seat/month with seat minimums; free-tier availability is inconsistent across sources.

one_liner: Omnichannel helpdesk from Quality Unit with ticketing, live chat, and call center.
auth_notes: API v3 uses per-key API keys created in Configuration > System > API, with per-key permission scoping.
credential_path: Start a 30-day trial, then in the agent panel go to Configuration > System > API and add a new API key with permissions.
breadth_note: Tickets, messages, contacts, agents, departments, companies, chats, calls, knowledge base.

mcp.note: Quality Unit (LiveAgent's vendor) publishes a built-in MCP server documented at support.liveagent.com/647358; connects Claude/Cursor using the agent's own identity and permissions.

rate_limits: 180 requests per minute per API key
blocker: API v3 reference is served only inside your own tenant (<domain>.ladesk.com/docs/api/v3), so schemas are hard to survey pre-signup.
notes: Unconfirmed: whether API access is gated by plan tier, and the exact webhook model (appears to be rule/plugin driven rather than a subscription API).

one_liner: API-first support tool for technical B2B teams, built on a public GraphQL API.
auth_notes: GraphQL API key sent as Bearer with per-key permission scopes; outbound webhooks are HMAC-signed.
credential_path: Sign up for the free trial, then Settings > API Keys in your Plain workspace and create a key with the needed permissions.
breadth_note: Plain's own UI runs on the same GraphQL API: threads, customers, tenants, labels, email, chat, help center.

mcp.note: Plain hosts mcp.plain.com/mcp with roughly 30 tools spanning threads, customers, tenants, help center articles, and workspace data; supports reads and writes.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: GraphQL only, no REST, so a toolkit needs GraphQL codegen. Rate limits were not found in public docs; API region host is core-api.uk.plain.com.

one_liner: Simple shared inbox, knowledge base, and Beacon widget for small support teams.
auth_notes: Inbox/Mailbox API 2.0 is OAuth2 only: client credentials for internal apps, authorization code for multi-customer apps.
credential_path: On a paid plan, go to Your Profile > My Apps > Create My App to get client_id/client_secret, then POST to /v2/oauth2/token.
breadth_note: Conversations, threads, customers, mailboxes, users, tags, workflows, reports, plus a separate Docs API.

mcp.note: Help Scout runs a first-party server at mcp.helpscout.net/mcp, added as an OAuth custom connector; reported generally available to all customers. Community server drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server predates it.

rate_limits: ~200-800 req/min per account by plan; 429 with Retry-After
blocker: Free plan excludes API and integrations, so a paid seat is needed before any credentials work.
notes: Access tokens expire in about 48 hours (expires_in 172800), so a toolkit must handle refresh or re-issue via client credentials.

one_liner: Ecommerce-focused helpdesk deeply integrated with Shopify and DTC storefronts.
auth_notes: Private apps use HTTP Basic with account email plus API key; OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps other accounts install.
credential_path: In the helpdesk, Settings > Account > REST API shows your base API URL, username (email), and API key password.
breadth_note: Tickets, messages, customers, views, macros, rules, tags, integrations, satisfaction surveys, events, jobs.

mcp.note: First-party connector at mcp.gorgias.com/mcp, in open beta since around May 2026, reported free on every Helpdesk plan. Community servers also exist.

rate_limits: 40 req/20s for API keys; 80 req/20s for OAuth apps (leaky bucket)
notes: Public apps listed for other Gorgias merchants must use OAuth2 and go through Gorgias app listing; private API-key apps need no review.

one_liner: People-centered, customer-not-ticket service platform for enterprise retail and travel brands.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic using an agent-bound API token; the token is tied to a Gladly user holding the API User role.
credential_path: Requires an existing Gladly org obtained via sales demo; an admin grants the API User role, then creates a token in Settings > API Tokens.
breadth_note: Customers, conversations, conversation items, tasks, agents, topics, plus reporting and data export endpoints.

mcp.note: No first-party Gladly MCP server found. Third-party hosted connectors exist (StackOne reports ~65 actions; Truto offers a hosted connector for Claude).

rate_limits: 10 requests per second per organization by default
blocker: No self-serve signup, no published pricing, no trial; credentials require an already-provisioned enterprise Gladly org.
notes: Unconfirmed: whether Gladly exposes outbound webhooks/event streams, and whether any ISV or partner program gates production API use.

one_liner: Team messaging platform with channels, bots, and a deep Web API.
auth_notes: OAuth v2 issues bot (xoxb) and user (xoxp) tokens; inbound Events/Interactivity requests verified via signing-secret HMAC.
credential_path: Create app at api.slack.com/apps, add bot/user scopes, install to your workspace, copy bot token; enable distribution for multi-workspace OAuth.
breadth_note: 200+ Web API methods: chat, conversations, users, files, canvases, lists, admin, workflows.

mcp.note: Slack-hosted remote MCP at mcp.slack.com/mcp, GA 17 Feb 2026; workspace admins approve which MCP clients connect.

rate_limits: Per-method tiers; non-Marketplace apps 1 req/min on conversations.history
blocker: Distributed non-Marketplace apps throttled to 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history/replies.
notes: Credentials are free and instant. Real gate is Marketplace review, which restores normal history rate limits; internal custom apps exempt.

one_liner: Programmable SMS, voice, video, and verification APIs for developers.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic using Account SID plus Auth Token, or API Key SID/secret; JWT access tokens for client SDKs; signed webhooks.
credential_path: Sign up at twilio.com, verify email and phone; Account SID and Auth Token appear in Console; create API keys under Account settings.
breadth_note: Roughly 1,800 endpoints across 30+ products: Messaging, Voice, Verify, Lookup, Studio, Serverless.

mcp.note: twilio-labs/mcp, public beta, generated from Twilio OpenAPI specs; runs via npx with Account SID and API key.

rate_limits: Per-product concurrency and throughput caps; documented per product
notes: Trial account works immediately; production US SMS additionally needs A2P 10DLC brand/campaign registration, which was not re-verified in this pass.

one_liner: Zoho's team chat app with channels, bots, and REST APIs.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 only; access token sent as bearer. Self Client option generates tokens for your own account without a user flow.
credential_path: Register a client (or Self Client) in Zoho API Console, choose scopes, generate grant code, exchange for access and refresh tokens.
breadth_note: Chats, channels, messages, users, buddies, files, bots; plus Cliq Platform bots, widgets, commands.

mcp.note: Zoho markets an official Cliq MCP server exposing channels, threads, users and history; endpoint URL and auth details not published on the public help page.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Unconfirmed: Cliq-specific rate limits and MCP endpoint/auth. Also must handle per-data-center domains (.com, .eu, .in) when exchanging tokens.

one_liner: Lark collaboration suite: messaging, docs, calendar, Base, broad open APIs.
auth_notes: App ID and secret exchange for app_access_token and tenant_access_token; user OAuth yields user_access_token. All sent as bearer.
credential_path: Create a custom app in the open.larksuite.com developer console, request permission scopes, submit for tenant admin review, then release.
breadth_note: Messaging, contacts, calendar, Docs, Base/Bitable, Drive, approval, attendance, meeting rooms.

mcp.note: Official @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp wraps nearly the whole OpenAPI surface; file upload/download and direct doc editing unsupported.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint frequency limits documented per API; specific values unverified
blocker: Tenant admin must approve requested scopes and release the app before any API call succeeds.
notes: Lark (international) and Feishu (China) are separate tenants with separate consoles and domains. Store-listed apps face an additional Lark review.

one_liner: CAKE.com's Slack alternative, with API exposed through an API Keys addon.
auth_notes: Workspace API key passed in the ApiKey request header; generated in the API sidebar or via the /api-keys generate slash command.
credential_path: Enable the API Keys addon, open API in the left sidebar, click Add API key, name it, Generate; or run /api-keys generate.
breadth_note: Send/delete messages, reactions, replies, create and list channels, DMs, history, users.

mcp.note: Community wrappers only (infralayers/pumble-mcp, apet97/pumble-python-sdk); no MCP server published by Pumble or CAKE.com.

rate_limits: 1000 requests per minute per user
blocker: Narrow endpoint surface, addon must be enabled, and no documented events or webhooks for inbound triggers.
notes: Help page says the addon is available on all plans. Unconfirmed: webhook/event support and whether OAuth exists for multi-tenant installs.

one_liner: Community chat platform with bot, OAuth2, gateway, and interactions APIs.
auth_notes: Bot token in Authorization: Bot header; OAuth2 authorization code for user scopes; interaction endpoints verified with Ed25519 signatures.
credential_path: Create an application at discord.com/developers/applications, add a Bot, reset and copy the token, configure OAuth2 redirect and scopes.
breadth_note: Guilds, channels, messages, threads, members, roles, interactions, webhooks, voice, scheduled events.

mcp.note: Numerous community servers (SaseQ, hanweg, v-3, Docker MCP catalog); no Discord-operated official MCP server found.

rate_limits: Per-route buckets via X-RateLimit headers; global ~50 requests/second
blocker: Message Content and other privileged intents need verification approval once the bot exceeds 100 guilds.
notes: Token is instant and free. Growth gate: unverified bots stop joining new servers at 100 guilds, and privileged intents then require ID verification.

one_liner: Messaging app with a free token-based Bot API and MTProto client API.
auth_notes: Bot token from @BotFather embedded in the request URL path, not a header; MTProto client API needs api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org.
credential_path: Message @BotFather in any Telegram client, send /newbot, pick a name and username, receive the HTTP API token immediately.
breadth_note: Full Bot API: messages, media, chats, inline mode, payments, forums, stickers, business accounts.

mcp.note: Several community Bot API MCP servers (one exposes 174 tools); nothing official from Telegram.

rate_limits: ~30 msgs/sec global, 1/sec per chat, 20/min per group
notes: Lowest-friction app in this set. Bots cannot initiate chats with users, and Paid Broadcasts in BotFather raises the ceiling to 1000 msgs/sec.

one_liner: Meta's business messaging platform, delivered via Cloud API on Graph API.
auth_notes: Graph bearer tokens: 24-hour temp token, then permanent system user token; tech providers use OAuth Embedded Signup. Webhooks signed X-Hub-Signature-256.
credential_path: Create a Meta app with the WhatsApp use case, link a Business portfolio, use the test number, then system user token plus verification.
breadth_note: Send messages, templates, media, flows, phone number and WABA management; no general inbox history read.

mcp.note: Meta announced a WhatsApp Business Tools MCP in September 2026 for setup, templates and webhooks, positioned for dev/testing not production scale. Exact endpoint URL not verified.

rate_limits: Tiered 24h messaging limits (1K/10K/100K+) tied to verification and quality
blocker: Business Verification plus App Review for Advanced Access on whatsapp_business_messaging; dedicated phone number required.
notes: Cloud API is the practical path. Direct (own-business) use skips App Review; multi-tenant Tech Provider use does not. On-prem API status not re-verified.

one_liner: Cloud phone system for sales and support with a public REST API.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic using api_id as username and api_token as password; OAuth2 authorization_code with a single public_api scope for partner apps.
credential_path: As an admin, open Aircall Dashboard > Integrations & API > API keys, click Generate an API key, copy api_id and api_token immediately.
breadth_note: Calls, users, teams, numbers, contacts, tags, SMS/messaging, AI insights, webhooks.

mcp.note: Unofficial servers only (themobilefirstco ~73 tools, RosenAdvertising, plus Zapier/Pipedream hosted MCP); none from Aircall.

rate_limits: ~60 requests/minute per token; some sources cite 100/min
blocker: Requires a paid Aircall account and admin role; OAuth apps need Aircall Technology Partner onboarding.
notes: Conflicting sources on whether API access is all-plans or Professional-only, and on the exact rate limit. api_id is shown once and unrecoverable.

one_liner: Programmable voice, SMS, messaging, and verification APIs from Ericsson.
auth_notes: API key and secret (Basic) at account level; RS256 JWT signed with an Application private key, with application_id, iat, exp, jti claims.
credential_path: Sign up for a Vonage account; API key and secret appear in the Dashboard; create an Application to generate a public/private key pair.
breadth_note: SMS, Messages (WhatsApp/Viber/MMS), Voice with NCCO, Verify, Video, Numbers, Reports.

mcp.note: Vonage ships a Documentation MCP server plus an API Bindings MCP server covering reports, number management and application creation.

rate_limits: Messages API 75 requests/second per API key; other products vary
notes: JWT auth is recommended for production and is required for Voice and most Messages features; Basic auth alone is account-level only.

one_liner: Google's advertising platform API for campaigns, reporting, and bulk automation.
auth_notes: OAuth2 user or service account, plus required developer-token header and login-customer-id for manager accounts.
credential_path: Create Google Ads manager account, get test developer token in API Center, apply for Basic/Standard access.
breadth_note: Full campaign, ad group, keyword, audience, asset, budget, and GAQL reporting coverage.

mcp.note: Official Google-maintained MCP server, strictly read-only: list_accessible_customers, GAQL search, get_resource_metadata.

rate_limits: Test/Basic 15,000 ops/day; Explorer 2,880/day; Standard unlimited.
blocker: Developer token required; Basic access gated by review, Standard needs detailed manual compliance audit.
notes: Tiers now Test/Explorer/Basic/Standard. Explorer permits limited production calls without full Basic review; RMF applies only at Standard.

one_liner: Facebook and Instagram ads management through the Meta Marketing/Graph API.
auth_notes: OAuth2 via Facebook Login; long-lived user or Business Manager system-user tokens; appsecret_proof signing recommended.
credential_path: Create Meta app, add Marketing API, complete Business Verification, submit App Review for ads_management Advanced Access.
breadth_note: Campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, custom audiences, insights, catalogs, pixels, Conversions API.

mcp.note: Meta shipped an official ads MCP server plus CLI in 2026, branded AI connectors; OAuth-gated read and write.

rate_limits: Tiered per app; business-use-case throttles surfaced via X-Business-Use-Case-Usage headers.
blocker: App Review plus Business Verification for ads_management Advanced Access, and a separate Marketing API access tier.
notes: Two independent gates: per-permission App Review/Advanced Access, and the Marketing API Access Tier (formerly Ads Management Standard Access).

one_liner: LinkedIn advertising campaign management and reporting via the Marketing API.
auth_notes: OAuth2 3-legged member auth for ads endpoints; 2-legged client credentials for some app-auth calls; versioned headers required.
credential_path: Create LinkedIn developer app, add Advertising API product, submit Access Request Form; LinkedIn vets business and use case.
breadth_note: Campaign groups, campaigns, creatives, matched audiences, lead gen forms, conversions, analytics reporting.

mcp.note: No official LinkedIn MCP server as of mid-2026; community and hosted servers wrap the public Marketing API.

rate_limits: Daily application and member quotas per endpoint, reset midnight UTC; 429 on throttle.
blocker: Advertising API access requires LinkedIn developer and application vetting; approvals commonly reported as weeks to months.
notes: Hardest gate in this category: no usable sandbox before approval, and webhooks only for applications with an approved webhook use case.

one_liner: White-label agency CRM, funnels, and marketing automation platform API.
auth_notes: API v2 uses OAuth2 authorization code for marketplace apps, or Private Integration Tokens for internal single-account use.
credential_path: Paid HighLevel account; generate Private Integration Token in Settings, or create an OAuth app in the developer marketplace.
breadth_note: Contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, workflows, forms, social planner, email templates.

mcp.note: Official LeadConnector MCP endpoint at services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/, authenticated by OAuth or Private Integration Token.

rate_limits: Documented burst and daily per-app/location caps; exact numbers not verified here.
blocker: Requires a paid HighLevel subscription; public marketplace distribution needs app review including a Loom demo.
notes: Private Integration Tokens allow building immediately with no review; review applies only to public marketplace distribution. Rate-limit numbers unconfirmed.

one_liner: Email marketing platform with audiences, campaigns, automations, and reporting.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic with an API key (any username), or OAuth2 to act on other users' accounts; datacenter prefix required.
credential_path: Sign up free, generate an API key under Account > Extras > API keys; OAuth app registration is self-serve.
breadth_note: Audiences, members, campaigns, templates, automations, reports, e-commerce stores, landing pages.

mcp.note: Official MCP documented for Transactional (Mandrill) at mandrillapp.com/mcp; Marketing API MCP coverage is largely community servers.

rate_limits: Ten simultaneous connections per API key; no documented per-minute request rate.
notes: OAuth2 is required only for Marketplace listing via the Integration Partner Program; an API key is sufficient for a private toolkit.

one_liner: Ecommerce email and SMS marketing platform with profiles, flows, campaigns.
auth_notes: Scoped private API key in a Klaviyo-API-Key header, or OAuth2 for tech-partner apps; public key for client-side.
credential_path: Create a Klaviyo account, generate a scoped private API key in Settings > API keys; OAuth app setup is self-serve.
breadth_note: Profiles, lists, segments, events, campaigns, flows, templates, catalogs, metrics, coupons, reporting.

mcp.note: Official remote MCP at mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp with OAuth, plus a local MCP authenticated by a scoped private API key.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint burst and steady buckets; OAuth apps get separate quota per install.
notes: Cleanest agent story in this category. Max ten webhooks per account; webhook topics require matching read scopes such as events:read.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder, email marketing, and online course platform.
auth_notes: API key generated in profile settings under Public API keys; up to three keys per account; sent as a request header.
credential_path: Sign up (free plan available), open profile settings, create a key in the Public API keys section.
breadth_note: Contacts, tags, custom fields, funnels, sales, email campaigns; no ads or deep analytics endpoints.

mcp.note: Official MCP server with dedicated MCP keys created in Settings; covers contacts, newsletters, and email campaigns.

rate_limits: Returns 429 with a Retry-After header; exact quota not published.
notes: Smallest surface of the ten but fully self-serve, with an llms.txt and OpenAPI index. Exact header name and rate limits unconfirmed.

one_liner: Pins, boards, ads, and analytics through the Pinterest REST API v5.
auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code with scoped access and refresh tokens; app credentials used for the token exchange.
credential_path: Register a Pinterest business account and app, get approved for Trial access, then apply for Standard with a demo video.
breadth_note: Pins, boards, user account, ads, ad groups, audiences, analytics, catalogs, conversions.

mcp.note: No official MCP for the public Pinterest API; community servers wrap API v5. Pinterest's own MCP ecosystem is internal only.

rate_limits: Trial: per-day per-app. Standard: per-minute, per-user, per-app, higher limits.
blocker: Trial access produces sandbox-only Pins and Boards; Standard access needs review with an OAuth flow demo video.
notes: Access tiers confirmed from official docs. Webhook support is not documented on developers.pinterest.com and the 'no' here is unconfirmed.

one_liner: Meta's text social network API for publishing posts, replies, and insights.
auth_notes: Threads OAuth2; short-lived one-hour tokens exchanged for 60-day long-lived tokens that must be refreshed.
credential_path: Create a Meta app with the Threads use case; self-serve for own and tester accounts, App Review for public users.
breadth_note: Publish posts and replies, read own media, insights, mentions, keyword search.

mcp.note: No official Threads MCP server; multiple unofficial servers wrap the Threads Graph API, plus scraper-based Apify actors.

rate_limits: 250 posts, 1,000 replies, 100 deletions per profile per 24 hours.
blocker: Serving non-tester users requires per-permission Meta App Review with screencast, and often business verification.
notes: API is free. Own-account and tester builds work immediately; multi-tenant needs App Review. Webhook support not confirmed in sources retrieved.

one_liner: Twilio's transactional and marketing email API with deliverability tooling.
auth_notes: Bearer API key with granular scopes created in SendGrid settings; the same key also authenticates SMTP relay.
credential_path: Sign up for a SendGrid/Twilio account, verify sender identity, create a scoped API key under Settings > API Keys.
breadth_note: Mail send, dynamic templates, contacts, marketing campaigns, stats, suppressions, domain authentication, subusers.

mcp.note: No official SendGrid MCP; Twilio's official MCP wraps Twilio's Public API only. Twilio published a build-your-own tutorial.

rate_limits: Roughly 600 requests/minute on most v3 endpoints; mail/send largely unthrottled; 429 on excess.
notes: Perpetual free tier is gone; now a 60-day, 100-emails-per-day trial then Essentials from $19.95/mo. Rate-limit figure from secondary sources.

one_liner: Hosted ecommerce platform with deep Admin, Storefront and Functions APIs.
auth_notes: Admin-created custom apps issue a static Admin API token; Partner/Dev-dashboard custom and public apps use OAuth2; webhooks HMAC-signed.
credential_path: Free Partner account plus dev store, or merchant admin Settings > Apps > Develop apps to mint a token.
breadth_note: Products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, discounts, metafields, B2B, Functions; GraphQL Admin is the primary surface.

mcp.note: Official @shopify/dev-mcp (docs/schema introspection, no auth) plus an official Storefront MCP server for shopper agents.

rate_limits: GraphQL leaky bucket 1000 points, 50/sec restore; plan-scaled
notes: Shopify removed admin-created custom apps; the single-store path is now a Dev Dashboard/CLI app with custom distribution (no Shopify review).

one_liner: Open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin exposing a self-hosted REST API.
auth_notes: Consumer key/secret over HTTPS as HTTP Basic; OAuth 1.0a one-legged HMAC-SHA1/256 for non-SSL sites.
credential_path: Store admin generates keys at WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API; no vendor approval.
breadth_note: Products, variations, orders, refunds, customers, coupons, reports, taxes, shipping, settings, webhooks.

mcp.note: Native MCP support shipped in WooCommerce core but is in developer preview; several community servers also exist.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Self-hosted, so base URL is per-store and limits depend on the host, not WooCommerce. Some servers mangle the Authorization header.

one_liner: SaaS ecommerce platform with API-first catalog, orders and storefront APIs.
auth_notes: Store-level API accounts issue non-expiring tokens sent as X-Auth-Token; marketplace apps use OAuth2 with scopes.
credential_path: Store control panel Settings > Store-level API accounts; app developers register free at devtools.bigcommerce.com.
breadth_note: Catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkout, pricing, channels; GraphQL Storefront and Admin surfaces.

mcp.note: Storefront MCP server in beta, enabled per-store by the owner via Early Access; docs site also exposes an MCP endpoint.

rate_limits: Quota per 30s window, plan-scaled (~450 for standard)
notes: Store-level token is the simplest connector path. Enterprise plans can get an unlimited rate plan. Storefront MCP is beta, not GA.

one_liner: Enterprise B2C/B2B commerce suite behind Salesforce licensing and Account Manager.
auth_notes: Account Manager client ID/secret OAuth2 for SCAPI Admin and OCAPI; SLAS issues shopper tokens. Separate client IDs per framework.
credential_path: Requires a licensed B2C Commerce realm or ISV partner enrollment; admin creates API client in Account Manager.
breadth_note: SCAPI Shopper and Admin APIs plus legacy OCAPI: products, orders, customers, promotions, catalogs, sandbox management.

mcp.note: No official Salesforce Commerce MCP server confirmed; a community commercecloud-mcp-server exists.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: No free self-serve sandbox; needs a license or B2C Commerce partner enrollment to obtain credentials.
notes: On-demand sandboxes require purchased credits; a 90-day trial sandbox exists only for B2C Commerce ISV prospects. Rate limits unverified.

one_liner: Adobe's enterprise commerce platform; Magento Open Source is the free self-hosted edition.
auth_notes: Integration tokens and admin/customer bearer tokens; OAuth 1.0a for integrations; Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses Adobe IMS OAuth2.
credential_path: Admin creates an Integration under System > Integrations for a token; Adobe-hosted editions need an Adobe license and IMS credentials.
breadth_note: Catalog, orders, carts/quotes, customers, inventory/MSI, CMS, shipping, tax; GraphQL is storefront-focused.

mcp.note: Adobe announced a Commerce MCP server at Summit 2026 per third-party reporting; I could not confirm it on an Adobe-owned page. Third-party CData server exists.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: Adobe Commerce is license-gated with no free self-serve sandbox; testing realistically means self-hosting Magento Open Source.
notes: Auth model differs sharply between self-hosted (integration tokens) and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (IMS). Official MCP status unconfirmed.

one_liner: Website builder whose Commerce APIs cover orders, products and inventory.
auth_notes: Per-site API keys with per-API read/write permissions, or OAuth2 for Squarespace Extensions distributed to any-plan merchants.
credential_path: API keys require a Commerce Advanced plan; generated in site Settings > Developer API Keys. OAuth needs Extension registration.
breadth_note: Orders, Products, Inventory, Transactions, Contacts, Discounts, Analytics, Forms, Webhook Subscriptions. No cart/checkout write.

mcp.note: No official Squarespace MCP server found in prior searches; could not run a dedicated search before the budget ran out.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: API keys gated behind Commerce Advanced plan; Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth-only, not available to API keys.
notes: Plan naming varies across sources (Business vs Commerce Advanced vs Core/Plus/Advanced); official auth page says Commerce Advanced for API keys.

one_liner: Lightspeed's embeddable store widget with a REST API and app platform.
auth_notes: OAuth2 with client_id/client_secret; non-expiring secret access tokens for backend use. Store ID now required for external app auth.
credential_path: Store admin creates a custom app under Ecwid admin > Apps > develop-apps to get client_id/secret; scope changes need a request form.
breadth_note: Products, categories, orders, customers, discount coupons, store profile, batch requests, storefront JS API.

mcp.note: No official Ecwid/Lightspeed MCP server found; dedicated search not run before the web search budget was exhausted.

rate_limits: 600 requests/minute per token; 429 with Retry-After
blocker: Public/multi-store apps need Ecwid review; scope or endpoint changes go through a contact form rather than self-serve.
notes: Docs are split across api-docs.ecwid.com and newer docs.ecwid.com. Webhook retries back off over 24 hours then drop.

one_liner: Creator storefront for digital products, with a small OAuth2 REST API.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0; sellers can self-generate a non-expiring personal access token from their own application record.
credential_path: Create an application at gumroad.com/oauth/applications, then click Generate access token for own-account use.
breadth_note: Products, variants, offer codes, sales, subscribers, license verification, user; no catalog-wide storefront or checkout control.

mcp.note: No official Gumroad MCP server found; community gumroad-mcp-server implementations are listed on MCP directories.

rate_limits: undocumented; 429s observed, no published numbers
notes: Webhooks are 'resource subscriptions' (sale, refund, dispute, cancellation, subscription_*). Did not fetch the primary gumroad.com/api reference directly.

one_liner: Amazon's seller/vendor API for listings, orders, fulfillment, reports and finances.
auth_notes: Login with Amazon OAuth2; LWA client credentials plus a refresh token per selling partner. Restricted data needs extra RDT tokens.
credential_path: Register a developer/solution provider profile, get Amazon approval, then register the app in Solution Provider Portal for LWA credentials.
breadth_note: Orders, listings, catalog, FBA inventory and inbound, reports, feeds, finances, pricing, shipping, notifications.

mcp.note: Amazon publishes an official SP-API dev/workflow MCP package in its samples repo; numerous community servers also exist.

rate_limits: Token bucket per operation; most ~1-5 req/sec with burst
blocker: Developer profile review plus per-role qualification; public apps must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore.
notes: Notifications are delivered via SQS/EventBridge rather than plain HTTP webhooks. Role approval, not just app registration, is the real gate.

one_liner: Creator commerce and payments platform, rebranded to Commas.
auth_notes: Scoped API key sent in an x-api-key header per a mirrored copy of the docs; separate sandbox key required. Not verified on a first-party page.
credential_path: Keys appear to be issued from the seller account dashboard; no public self-serve signup-to-key path was confirmed.
breadth_note: Checkout sessions, customers, subscribers, products, transactions, refunds, discount codes, invoices, disputes.

mcp.note: No FanBasis/Commas MCP server found in any search result.

rate_limits: ~10,000/hour on checkout-sessions and customers only (unverified)
blocker: Credential issuance appears account-gated with no public developer signup; rebrand to Commas is mid-flight.
notes: fanbasis.com 301-redirects to commas.com - the product rebranded to Commas. Marketing mentions APIs and SDKs; no developer docs or key issuance exist.

one_liner: Pay-as-you-go SEO data APIs for SERP, keywords, backlinks and on-page.
auth_notes: HTTP Basic with account email plus a dedicated API password; base64 Authorization header on every call.
credential_path: Self-serve signup, then copy API login/password from dashboard; free trial plus sandbox endpoints available.
breadth_note: Seven-plus API families: SERP, Keywords Data, Labs, Backlinks, OnPage, Business Data, Domain Analytics.

mcp.note: Official v3 TypeScript MCP server; earlier v2 server deprecated in a separate repo.

rate_limits: ~2,000 requests/min general; some endpoints far lower
notes: Cleanest build target in the category: documented Basic auth, sandbox, postback/pingback callbacks, official MCP server.

one_liner: SEO platform exposing a Data API and a project-management Project API.
auth_notes: Single API key works across both APIs; sent as Authorization: Token <key>, or an apikey query parameter.
credential_path: Create key in-app via API dashboard 'Create API key'; works on free trial and paid subscriptions.
breadth_note: Data API for raw SEO/AEO datasets plus Project API for rank tracking, audits and project CRUD.

mcp.note: Official MCP server documented under integrations; official Claude skills catalogue at github.com/seranking/seo-skills.

rate_limits: ~10 rps Data API, ~5 rps Project API; trial 1 rps
notes: Rate-limit figures partly sourced from MCP server description; webhook support not confirmed in docs reviewed.

one_liner: Backlink and keyword intelligence API metered in per-plan API units.
auth_notes: API v3 keys created by workspace owners/admins in account settings; MCP uses separate MCP keys as bearer tokens.
credential_path: Owner/admin creates key in Ahrefs account settings; requires an eligible paid plan, plus limited free test queries.
breadth_note: Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, Rank Tracker, Site Audit, brand/AI visibility, management endpoints; OpenAPI spec published.

mcp.note: Remote official MCP server; the older local repo github.com/ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server is archived and outdated.

rate_limits: 60 requests/min default; dynamic throttling; API units per plan
blocker: Paid plan required and every billable call burns non-refundable units (50-unit minimum).
notes: Correction to older assumptions: API is no longer Enterprise-only, it is 'available on eligible paid plans' with free test queries.

one_liner: AI web scraper with API, SDKs, CLI and rotating residential proxies.
auth_notes: API token created in dashboard account settings (API Tokens page) and sent as a bearer token.
credential_path: Self-serve signup, no card; free tier includes 1,000 tokens and API-based scraping, token from account settings.
breadth_note: Scraper run/endpoint activation, results retrieval, plus Python/Node SDKs, LangChain integration and CLI.

mcp.note: Docs index lists an official MrScraper MCP server page under getting-started; exact endpoint URL not verified (page 404'd on direct fetch).

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Webhooks confirmed in docs index; no rate-limit page found. Hosted MCP endpoint URL unconfirmed. Paid plans unlock webhooks/workflows.

one_liner: Actor marketplace and cloud runtime for scrapers, with full platform API.
auth_notes: Apify API token from Console API & Integrations page as bearer; MCP server also supports browser OAuth sign-in.
credential_path: Self-serve signup, copy API token from Apify Console API & Integrations page; free plan credits available.
breadth_note: Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, request queues, builds, tasks, schedules, webhooks, billing.

mcp.note: Official hosted server at https://mcp.apify.com; four discovery/docs tools usable unauthenticated.

rate_limits: ~30 requests/sec per user on MCP; 429 with retry guidance
notes: Official MCP confirmed. Webhooks, schedules, request queues and tasks are REST-only features per Apify docs.

one_liner: LLM-ready scrape, crawl, map, search and extract API for agents.
auth_notes: fc- prefixed API key sent as Authorization: Bearer; MCP additionally offers OAuth sign-in and limited keyless access.
credential_path: Self-serve signup with no card; 1,000 free credits/month, key from firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys.
breadth_note: Scrape, crawl, map, search, extract, agent and monitor endpoints plus Node/Python SDKs.

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (and /v2/mcp-oauth); keyless mode with daily limits.

rate_limits: Free 10/min scrape, 2/min crawl; scales to 10,000/min
notes: Webhooks cover crawl, batch scrape, extract, agent and monitor events with retry backoff and auto-deactivation.

one_liner: Proxy network plus Web Unlocker, SERP, Scraper APIs and Browser API.
auth_notes: API token from account user settings used as bearer; proxy zones additionally use username/password proxy credentials.
credential_path: Self-serve signup; 5,000 free credits/month with no card, token from user settings page.
breadth_note: Web Unlocker, SERP API, Web Scraper API across 40+ site extractors, Scraping Browser, zone management, datasets.

mcp.note: Official MCP server exposing Web Unlocker, SERP, structured extractors and remote Scraping Browser; API_TOKEN env var.

rate_limits: Scraper API trigger 20/min, 60/hour; zone concurrency limits
notes: Rate-limit model is per-zone concurrency rather than global RPM; card may be required as verification beyond free credits.

one_liner: Open-source CLI that hunts usernames across 400+ social networks.
auth_notes: No accounts, no API keys, no hosted service; it queries public profile URLs directly from the local machine.
credential_path: No credentials exist; install via pipx install sherlock-project or the official Docker image.
breadth_note: Single capability: username-to-profile enumeration, output to CSV/JSON/txt. No server-side API surface.

mcp.note: Community FastMCP wrapper around the CLI; other community wrappers exist on Apify and in OSINT MCP bundles.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: No hosted API and no credentials to connect; CLI must be self-hosted and wrapped.
notes: MIT-licensed local tool. A connector is only possible by self-hosting the CLI behind your own service; nothing to authenticate against.

one_liner: Aggregates 30+ B2B data vendors behind one contact-enrichment API.
auth_notes: API key passed in the x-api-key header; an API-key management endpoint exists but key issuance process is undocumented.
credential_path: No self-serve signup found; site's only CTA is 'Book a Call'. Key provisioning appears sales/onboarding-led.
breadth_note: About 13 services: contact prospecting/enrichment, company search, email verify, phone enrich, job-change detection.

mcp.note: No official MCP server found. Docs do reference an 'Agent Skills' section for coding agents.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: No self-serve signup or public pricing; API key requires sales contact.
notes: Public API docs do exist at docs.waterfall.io/v1 (base https://api.waterfall.io), contradicting 'no public docs'; access path is the blocker.

one_liner: GTM data platform; public developer API shipped mid-2026.
auth_notes: API key in the clay-api-key header; created in Settings > Account > API keys (beta) or via the clay CLI.
credential_path: Create key in Clay settings or 'clay api-keys create'; available on free, trial and paid plans.
breadth_note: Searches, Routines, Tables (read-only), Workflows (alpha), Me, Credits; inbound/outbound webhooks for row data.

mcp.note: Docs mention using Clay with 'MCP clients' and ship a coding-agent plugin/CLI, but no dedicated MCP server page found.

rate_limits: Documented rate-limits page; free 100 search results/month
blocker: Tables are read-only; structured table queries and paging past 100 rows need Enterprise API table sync.
notes: Updates the old 'no public API' assumption: a public API now exists, but write access to tables is still absent.

one_liner: Code hosting, pull requests, issues, Actions CI and package registry.
auth_notes: Fine-grained or classic PAT, OAuth app, or GitHub App (JWT to installation token). Bearer header on all REST calls.
credential_path: Free account, Settings > Developer settings > PAT; GitHub App or OAuth app registration is also self-serve.
breadth_note: Hundreds of REST endpoints plus full GraphQL v4 covering repos, issues, PRs, Actions, orgs, security.

mcp.note: Official local server plus GA remote endpoint api.githubcopilot.com/mcp with OAuth.

rate_limits: 5,000/hr authenticated; 60/hr unauthenticated; 15,000/hr Enterprise Apps
notes: Reference-grade developer API. GitHub App installation tokens are the right pattern for multi-tenant toolkits.

one_liner: Frontend hosting platform for deployments, projects, domains and edge functions.
auth_notes: Access token in Authorization: Bearer header; OAuth2 available for marketplace integrations acting on user teams.
credential_path: Free Hobby account, then Account Settings > Tokens > Create Token; scope to a team if needed.
breadth_note: Deployments, projects, env vars, domains, DNS, teams, logs, edge config, firewall and analytics.

mcp.note: Official hosted remote server at mcp.vercel.com with OAuth; shipped public beta then expanded.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint; X-RateLimit-* headers, 429 with Retry-After
notes: Team-scoped tokens matter: most endpoints need a teamId query param for org resources. Exact per-endpoint limits unconfirmed.

one_liner: Jamstack hosting for sites, deploys, forms, functions and DNS.
auth_notes: Personal access token as Authorization: Bearer; OAuth2 required for public multi-user integrations.
credential_path: Free account, then Applications > Personal access tokens > New access token.
breadth_note: OpenAPI-described: sites, deploys, builds, forms, submissions, DNS zones, env vars, teams, hooks.

mcp.note: Official server; docs at docs.netlify.com/build/build-with-ai/netlify-mcp-server and a hosted remote endpoint.

rate_limits: 500 requests/minute for most endpoints; stricter on some operations
notes: Deploy-creation endpoints have tighter limits than the 500/min default. OAuth app registration is self-serve for public integrations.

one_liner: CDN, DNS, WAF, Workers, R2 and Zero Trust edge platform.
auth_notes: Scoped API tokens via Authorization: Bearer (preferred); legacy global API key with X-Auth-Email/X-Auth-Key. OAuth used by MCP servers.
credential_path: Free account, then My Profile > API Tokens > Create Token with scoped account/zone permissions.
breadth_note: Very large surface: zones, DNS, WAF, Workers, KV, R2, D1, Pages, Access; GraphQL analytics separately.

mcp.note: Catalog of managed remote servers (*.mcp.cloudflare.com) with OAuth; repos cloudflare/mcp and mcp-server-cloudflare.

rate_limits: 1,200 requests per 5 minutes per user, account-wide cumulative
notes: 1,200/5min limit is cumulative across dashboard and all tokens, so it bites in agent loops. Notification webhooks not directly reconfirmed.

one_liner: Hosted Postgres with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions.
auth_notes: Management API uses personal access token (Bearer) or OAuth2; per-project data APIs use anon/service_role keys and user JWTs.
credential_path: Free account, then Account Settings > Access Tokens; scoped PATs in public alpha, classic PATs are full-access.
breadth_note: Management API for projects, orgs, branches, secrets, functions; per-project PostgREST plus pg_graphql and realtime.

mcp.note: Hosted server at mcp.supabase.com/mcp with OAuth dynamic client registration; PAT fallback for CI. Repo github.com/supabase/mcp.

rate_limits: Management API 60 requests/minute per user, scoped per project/org
notes: Two distinct API layers: control plane (Management API, PAT) and data plane (project URL + anon/service keys). Model both.

one_liner: Graph database; Cypher over Bolt/HTTP plus an Aura cloud management API.
auth_notes: Aura API: OAuth2 client_credentials to api.neo4j.io/oauth/token. Database Query API: HTTP Basic with DB username/password.
credential_path: Aura console > API credentials, but Free/Professional users must add billing info or marketplace project first.
breadth_note: Aura REST is instance/tenant lifecycle CRUD only; real work is Cypher over Bolt or the HTTP Query API.

mcp.note: Official server (get-schema, read-cypher, write-cypher, list-gds-procedures) using NEO4J_MCP_URI/USERNAME/PASSWORD; also neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j Labs servers.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: Not a SaaS REST app: needs DB connection credentials; Aura API credentials gated behind billing info on free tiers.
notes: Two separate things: open-source/self-hosted DB (Bolt or Query API /db/{name}/query/v2, Basic auth) vs Aura management REST API (OAuth2).

one_liner: Cloud data warehouse with SQL REST API and Cortex AI services.
auth_notes: Key-pair JWT (RS256, ~1hr, X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT) or Snowflake OAuth; PATs also supported.
credential_path: 30-day trial with $400 credits, no card at signup.snowflake.com; then generate RSA key pair and set user RSA_PUBLIC_KEY.
breadth_note: SQL API at /api/v2/statements plus object REST APIs for warehouses, databases, tasks, users, Cortex.

mcp.note: Snowflake-managed MCP server GA Nov 2025, OAuth + RBAC; plus Snowflake-Labs/mcp open-source server.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: Account-scoped URL, key-pair setup and warehouse/role config make onboarding heavier than a plain API key.
notes: Every call needs the account identifier host. Outbound webhook notification integrations exist but are not classic event webhooks; unconfirmed detail.

one_liner: Managed MongoDB clusters with a versioned Administration API.
auth_notes: Service accounts via OAuth2 client_credentials at /api/oauth/token (1hr bearer) — recommended; legacy API keys use HTTP Digest auth.
credential_path: Free M0 cluster account, then Organization Access Manager > Applications > Service Accounts (or legacy API keys).
breadth_note: Admin API v2 covers clusters, projects, orgs, users, backups, alerts, metrics, network access, billing.

mcp.note: Official MongoDB MCP Server, local (mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server) and Atlas-managed hosted variants.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: HTTP Digest (not Basic) for legacy keys — many HTTP clients need explicit digest support. Atlas Data API and App Services reached EOL Sep 30 2025.

one_liner: Observability platform for metrics, logs, traces, monitors and dashboards.
auth_notes: DD-API-KEY header for writes; reads additionally need DD-APPLICATION-KEY. OAuth2 for marketplace integrations and MCP.
credential_path: Account (free plan or 14-day trial), then Organization Settings > API Keys and Application Keys.
breadth_note: v1 and v2 REST across metrics, logs, events, monitors, dashboards, incidents, SLOs, users, RUM, security.

mcp.note: Official remote server at mcp.datadoghq.com (site-specific), OAuth2 or API+app keys; in Preview. Repo datadog-labs/mcp-server.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint; 250k events/min org limit; log intake not rate limited
notes: Two-key model (API + app key) is the main integration gotcha. Auth docs state no plan gating for API access, but per-plan limits unconfirmed.

one_liner: Error monitoring and performance tracing for application issues and releases.
auth_notes: Organization auth tokens (recommended) or personal tokens in Authorization: Bearer; internal/public integrations support OAuth-style installs.
credential_path: Free sentry.io account, then Settings > Developer Settings > Organization Tokens, or User Settings > Personal Tokens.
breadth_note: Projects, issues, events, releases, teams, orgs, alerts, discover queries, source maps, Seer.

mcp.note: Official first-party remote server at mcp.sentry.dev/mcp, OAuth-only on the hosted endpoint; self-host with a token.

rate_limits: Per-endpoint; X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-* headers; values undocumented
notes: Rate limits are enforced per caller identity, so minting extra tokens will not raise throughput. Numeric limits not published.

one_liner: Connected workspace for docs, wikis, and databases.
auth_notes: Internal connections use static bearer token; public connections use OAuth 2.0. Personal access tokens also supported.
credential_path: Create integration at notion.so/profile/integrations, copy token, share pages with it; OAuth for public apps.
breadth_note: Pages, blocks, databases/data sources, users, comments, search, file uploads.

mcp.note: Hosted remote server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp with OAuth; repo makenotion/notion-mcp-server.

rate_limits: ~3 req/sec average per integration; per-workspace limit also applies
notes: Content must be explicitly shared with the integration; that sharing step is the main onboarding friction for agents.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid for building relational team apps.
auth_notes: Legacy API keys fully deprecated Feb 2024. Only scoped personal access tokens and OAuth remain.
credential_path: Create scoped PAT at airtable.com/create/tokens; register OAuth integration in developer hub for third-party apps.
breadth_note: Records CRUD, base/table/field schema, comments, attachments, webhooks, enterprise admin endpoints.

mcp.note: Airtable-org CLI targeting hosted https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp; explicitly labeled experimental.

rate_limits: 5 requests/second per base; not raised by higher plans
notes: Confirmed: API keys dead since Feb 2024, PAT/OAuth only. 5 rps per base is the practical ceiling for bulk agents.

one_liner: Issue tracking and project planning for software teams.
auth_notes: Personal API keys with selectable scopes, or OAuth2 for multi-user apps; both sent as Authorization header.
credential_path: Settings > Account > Security & Access to create a personal API key; OAuth app via workspace API settings.
breadth_note: Issues, projects, initiatives, cycles, teams, comments, labels, documents, attachments.

mcp.note: Linear-hosted remote server at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp, OAuth per session, streamable HTTP.

rate_limits: 2,500 requests/hour with API key; 600/hour unauthenticated
notes: GraphQL-only, no REST. Toolkit must hand-write operations or generate from schema; official SDK eases this.

one_liner: Atlassian issue tracking and agile project management platform.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 3LO for apps; Basic auth with email plus API token for scripts; PATs on Data Center.
credential_path: API token from id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens; OAuth 2.0 app via developer.atlassian.com console.
breadth_note: Issues, JQL search, projects, workflows, fields, users, permissions, attachments, agile boards/sprints.

mcp.note: Atlassian Rovo remote MCP covering Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass; OAuth 2.1 or API tokens.

rate_limits: Points-based hourly quota plus burst limits for 3LO/Forge/Connect apps
notes: OAuth apps calling api.atlassian.com need cloudId resolution first. Marketplace distribution adds app review, direct API does not.

one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects, and portfolios.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens for single-user scripts; OAuth 2.0 for apps acting on behalf of users.
credential_path: Create PAT in Asana developer console (app.asana.com/0/my-apps); register OAuth app in same console.
breadth_note: Tasks, projects, portfolios, goals, custom fields, sections, teams, users, attachments, search.

mcp.note: Asana-hosted V2 MCP server is GA with OAuth; V1 beta SSE endpoint deprecated, shutting down Aug 2026.

rate_limits: 150 req/min free plans, 1,500 req/min paid; search 60 req/min
notes: Webhook setup uses an X-Hook-Secret handshake, so the receiving endpoint must be live before registration succeeds.

one_liner: Visual work OS built on customizable boards and items.
auth_notes: Per-user API tokens from admin/member profile, or OAuth app tokens with scopes; short-lived tokens inside apps.
credential_path: Copy personal API token from monday profile > Developers > My access tokens; OAuth app via developer center.
breadth_note: Boards, items, columns, groups, subitems, docs, users, teams, updates, workspaces, files.

mcp.note: Hosted platform MCP at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp; API token, OAuth, or dynamic client registration.

rate_limits: Complexity budget 10M/min per account; 5-35 req/sec by plan tier
notes: GraphQL-only as expected. Complexity-point budgeting means query shape, not just call count, drives throttling.

one_liner: All-in-one productivity suite for tasks, docs, and goals.
auth_notes: Personal token prefixed pk_ sent raw in Authorization header, or OAuth 2.0 for distributed apps.
credential_path: Settings > Apps to generate personal API token; create OAuth app in same Apps settings page.
breadth_note: Tasks, lists, folders, spaces, docs, custom fields, time tracking, goals, comments, chat.

mcp.note: Hosted at https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp, public beta, OAuth-only; tight daily call caps without AI add-on.

rate_limits: 100 req/min free-Business; 1,000 Business Plus; 10,000 Enterprise
notes: 100 req/min on lower plans is restrictive for bulk sync. Note token goes in Authorization without a Bearer prefix.

one_liner: Doc-database hybrid combining text, tables, and automations.
auth_notes: Unscoped bearer API tokens inheriting user permissions; OAuth 2.0 supported for Packs and partner integrations.
credential_path: Generate API token from Coda account settings; free account sufficient for REST API access.
breadth_note: Docs, pages, tables, rows, columns, formulas, controls, automations, permissions; no deep block-level editing.

mcp.note: Official Coda/Superhuman Docs remote MCP in public beta; exact endpoint URL not confirmed from docs.

rate_limits: ~10 requests/second per token; varies by endpoint
blocker: Brand migration to Superhuman Docs is moving docs and endpoints; MCP endpoint unverified.
notes: Coda now redirects to docs.superhuman.com after the Superhuman/Grammarly acquisition. Webhooks are inbound automation triggers, not outbound event push.

one_liner: Enterprise work management on a familiar grid interface.
auth_notes: Personal bearer access tokens or OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow; token required in Authorization header.
credential_path: Generate API token in Personal Settings > API Access; requires Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management plan.
breadth_note: Sheets, rows, cells, columns, reports, dashboards, workspaces, attachments, users, groups, events.

mcp.note: Officially supported and generally available; also mirrored at github.com/smartsheet-platform/smar-mcp.

rate_limits: 300 requests/minute per token; heavy ops count as 10
blocker: API and MCP require Business+ plan, so free and Pro tier users cannot connect at all.
notes: Confirmed the plan gate: API access requires Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management. Pro and free tiers excluded.

one_liner: Time tracking, expenses, and invoicing for services teams.
auth_notes: PAT or OAuth2 bearer token plus mandatory Harvest-Account-Id header; User-Agent header also required.
credential_path: Create personal access token at id.getharvest.com/developers; copy account ID shown alongside the token.
breadth_note: Time entries, projects, tasks, clients, invoices, estimates, expenses, users, reports, time off.

mcp.note: No official server found; several independent community implementations wrap the v2 REST API.

rate_limits: 100 req/15 sec general; 100 req/15 min for Reports API
blocker: No webhooks, so change detection requires polling with updated_since filters.
notes: No webhooks: change detection must poll with updated_since. A constraint on toolkit design, not a blocker.

one_liner: Payments, billing and financial infrastructure API for internet businesses.
auth_notes: Secret or restricted API keys sent as Bearer; Connect platforms and the remote MCP server use OAuth2.
credential_path: Sign up at dashboard.stripe.com; test and live secret/restricted keys under Developers > API keys.
breadth_note: Hundreds of resources: PaymentIntents, subscriptions, invoices, Connect, Issuing, Payouts, Tax, Search.

mcp.note: Hosted remote server at mcp.stripe.com with OAuth; local server via npx -y @stripe/mcp (Stripe Agent Toolkit).

rate_limits: 100 req/s live, 25 req/s sandbox; per-endpoint caps
notes: Best-in-class case: instant self-serve keys, official MCP/agent toolkit, full OpenAPI, webhooks. Read-request allocations tied to transaction volume.

one_liner: Bank account linking with transactions, balances, identity and transfer data.
auth_notes: client_id and secret in request body or PLAID-CLIENT-ID / PLAID-SECRET headers; per-user access_tokens issued via Link.
credential_path: Dashboard signup returns Sandbox keys instantly; Production access needs a separate Dashboard request and approval.
breadth_note: Auth, Balance, Transactions, Identity, Investments, Liabilities, Transfer, Income, Identity Verification products.

mcp.note: Plaid-owned repo bundling prompts, sandbox data and an MCP aimed at building integrations, not at end-user account data.

rate_limits: Per-Item and per-client; /transactions/get 30/min per Item
blocker: Sandbox is self-serve but Production requires a Plaid review of use case and compliance.
notes: Sandbox keys are instant; Production requires a reviewed Dashboard request. The MCP is for building integrations, not reading account data.

one_liner: Global crypto exchange API for spot, futures, wallet and market data.
auth_notes: X-MBX-APIKEY header; SIGNED endpoints accept HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519 or RSA signatures over the query string.
credential_path: Generate API keys in Binance account settings after KYC; free testnet keys at testnet.binance.vision.
breadth_note: Spot, margin, futures, options, wallet, staking, sub-accounts; also WebSocket streams and FIX (no webhooks).

mcp.note: No Binance-owned MCP found; several unofficial servers exist, including a separate Binance.US one.

rate_limits: Weight-based, ~6000 request weight/min per IP; 429 then IP ban
blocker: Regional restrictions; Binance.US is a separate legal entity with its own docs, keys and endpoints.
notes: A toolkit must branch on global vs US entity. Trading endpoints are financially irreversible, so read-only scoping is advisable.

breadth_note: No public API surface confirmed for a product named Paygent Connect.

mcp.note: No MCP server found for any Paygent entity relevant to an NMI-powered gateway.

rate_limits: undocumented

notes: Product could not be identified by two independent passes. Candidates found: paygent.ai, paygent.co.jp, paygent.tech - none matching 'Paygent Connect (NMI-powered)'.

breadth_note: Four FX-audit tools only: check_fx_rate, audit_transaction, full_forensic_report, compare_fx_sources. No general REST reference.

mcp.note: Vendor-published MCP hosted on a Cloudflare worker; it proxies Twelve Data and Open Exchange Rates.

rate_limits: 3 free transaction audits per month per IP
blocker: No published API reference; ipayx.ai/docs returns 404, so the vendor MCP is the only usable surface.
notes: ipayx.ai/docs 404s (confirmed by fetch). Tool names, auth and pricing come from the vendor's own GitHub README, not a docs site.

one_liner: QuickBooks Online accounting API for invoices, customers, payments and reports.

credential_path: Free Intuit Developer account; create an app for Client ID/Secret plus a free sandbox company.
breadth_note: ~40 accounting entities plus reports, attachments and batch; separate Payments, Payroll and Time APIs.

mcp.note: Intuit-owned TypeScript MCP server for QuickBooks Online, ~389 stars at time of check.

rate_limits: ~500 req/min per realm, 10 concurrent; batch 40/min
notes: Rate limits and App Partner Program tiers ($300-$4,500/mo above a free 500k-read Builder tier) come from third-party blogs, not confirmed on Intuit's site.

one_liner: Cloud accounting API for invoices, contacts, bank transactions and reports.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code or PKCE; custom connections use client credentials scoped to one organisation.
credential_path: Free developer account at developer.xero.com; create an app for client ID/secret, test on the demo company.
breadth_note: Accounting, Payroll, Files, Projects, Assets, Bank Feeds and Finance APIs across many endpoints.

mcp.note: Maintained under the XeroAPI org; MIT licensed, custom-connection OAuth2 or bearer token.

rate_limits: 60/min and 5000/day per tenant; 5 concurrent calls
notes: Uncertified apps cap at 25 connected tenants and each org may connect only two uncertified apps; certification lifts both limits.

one_liner: Corporate card and spend management API for expenses, cards and transactions.
auth_notes: Dashboard-issued user tokens sent as Bearer; partner apps use OAuth2 authorization code, with client_credentials only for onboarding.
credential_path: Sign in to dashboard.brex.com as Account or Card Admin, Developer > Settings > Create Token with scopes.
breadth_note: Transactions, Expenses, Team/Cards, Budgets & Limits, Payments, Accounting, Travel, Onboarding and Webhooks APIs.

mcp.note: Hosted at api.brex.com/mcp with OAuth or API-key Bearer; 50+ tools; requires enabling a beta feature flag.

rate_limits: undocumented
blocker: Needs an existing Brex customer account with admin role; partner OAuth client IDs issued only on request.
notes: Confirmed: no self-serve developer signup. Partner docs say contact Brex developer support to be issued client ID and secret.

one_liner: Corporate card and spend API for transactions, bills and reimbursements.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 with granular scopes; client credentials for your own account, authorization code for third-party apps.
credential_path: Ramp dashboard Settings > Developer (admin required) creates an app; sandbox needs a separate access request form.
breadth_note: Transactions, cards, users, departments, bills, reimbursements, limits, accounting sync; published OpenAPI spec.

mcp.note: Ramp ships three MCP servers; the developer/docs one needs no account or key, account-data ones need OAuth.

rate_limits: 200 requests per 10-second rolling window per source IP
blocker: Needs an existing Ramp account with admin role; third-party production access requires Ramp approval.
notes: Docs are LLM-friendly (llms.txt, llms-api.txt, openapi/developer-api.json). Sandbox is a separate environment with its own base URL and credentials.

one_liner: Private capital markets data on companies, investors, funds and deals.

breadth_note: No public API reference located; only marketing pages for the platform and data products surfaced.

mcp.note: No PitchBook MCP server surfaced; not exhaustively searched because there is no underlying public API.

breadth_note: Enterprise-only notebook CRUD, sources, sharing, audio overviews; no consumer NotebookLM endpoints.

mcp.note: No official NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook MCP server found in Google documentation reviewed.

rate_limits: undocumented

notes: Consumer NotebookLM has no public API. Gemini Notebook Enterprise exposes Discovery Engine v1alpha notebook endpoints with a gcloud bearer token.

breadth_note: Channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, workspace and super-admin endpoints.

mcp.note: Official remote MCP documented in Otter help center; OAuth-only, read-only tools (search meetings, fetch transcript, user info). Rejects API keys.

rate_limits: 10 requests/second on Enterprise Public API
blocker: REST Public API gated to Enterprise workspaces; MCP alternative is read-only and OAuth-only.
notes: Inversion worth knowing: the official MCP server is available on the free Basic plan while the REST API is Enterprise-only.

one_liner: AI meeting recorder with public REST API, OAuth, webhooks and MCP.
auth_notes: Self-serve API key from User Settings API Access; OAuth 2.0 authorization code for distributed third-party apps.
credential_path: Generate key at fathom.video/customize#api-access-header; register an OAuth app for multi-tenant integrations.
breadth_note: Meetings, meeting types, recordings, summaries, transcripts, downloads, teams, members, users, webhooks.

mcp.note: Official MCP docs with ChatGPT and Claude setup pages; exact remote server endpoint not captured in retrieved pages.

rate_limits: 60 req/min standard; 30/min for transcripts, summaries, downloads
notes: FAQ states API keys and webhooks are included on all plans. Keys are user-scoped to own or shared meetings. Base: api.fathom.ai/external/v1.

one_liner: AI search over 220M research papers via self-serve REST API and MCP.
auth_notes: x-api-key header; keys self-issued from the API & MCP dashboard inside a Consensus account. No OAuth documented.
credential_path: Create key in Consensus account API & MCP dashboard; plan credits then $0.05 per call.
breadth_note: Essentially one search endpoint over 220M papers with rich filters; read-only, no writes.

mcp.note: Consensus markets an official MCP for Claude/ChatGPT/Copilot sharing the account and credits; remote server endpoint URL not confirmed.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Hint says 'OAuth requested' but documented auth is x-api-key only. docs.consensus.app returned 403; endpoint details from search snippets.

one_liner: Document parsing and extraction API with self-serve keys, SDKs and MCP.

credential_path: Sign up at studio.reducto.ai, create key under API Keys; free starter credits then usage billing.
breadth_note: Parse, extract, split, edit, upload plus async jobs; public OpenAPI 3.1 spec published.

mcp.note: Quickstart documents a Reducto MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and other coding agents; separate MCP endpoint URL not captured.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: Pricing roughly $10/1k pages parse and $20/1k extract, 20% async discount, ~15k free credits. Rate limits not published.

one_liner: Autonomous coding agent with broad REST API and official MCP server.

credential_path: Generate a service user or personal API key in Devin account settings; requires an active Devin account.
breadth_note: Sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets, schedules, attachments, repo wikis, enterprise analytics and user management.

mcp.note: Official Streamable-HTTP MCP with API-key auth; covers sessions, playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations and public/private repo wikis.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: v3 API at api.devin.ai/v3 with organization and enterprise scopes; v1/v2 still work. Webhook support and rate limits unconfirmed.

one_liner: Generative image and video suite with documented REST API, CLI and skills.
auth_notes: Header 'Authorization: Key <key_id>:<key_secret>' from cloud.higgsfield.ai; the CLI instead uses account login, no key.
credential_path: Create API key id/secret at cloud.higgsfield.ai; CLI path uses 'higgsfield auth login' and plan credits.
breadth_note: Async generative media endpoints: text/image-to-video, soul images, product photoshoot; poll or webhook for results.

mcp.note: Help center describes both an MCP for chat agents and CLI+skills for coding agents; MCP server endpoint URL not retrieved.

rate_limits: undocumented
notes: API docs confirm key/secret auth, base api.higgsfield.ai, async jobs, 7-day output retention. Full model endpoint list and rate limits not retrieved.

one_liner: Open-source npm CLI rendering Mermaid diagrams to SVG, PNG or PDF.
auth_notes: No authentication at all; runs locally via npm, npx, Docker or Podman. No hosted service exists.
credential_path: None. npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli, or use minlag/mermaid-cli Docker image.
breadth_note: Single mmdc command: diagram or markdown in, SVG/PNG/PDF out, with themes and transparent backgrounds.

mcp.note: No MCP server in the official repo. Third-party Mermaid MCP servers exist but were not verified in this pass.

rate_limits: none - runs entirely locally
notes: Correct finding: no auth, no hosted API. A toolkit wraps a local binary or container, not a remote service. Homebrew install discontinued.

one_liner: Third-party YouTube transcript, search and channel API with credit pricing.
auth_notes: Authorization: Bearer <api_key> from the account dashboard; 100 free credits granted on signup.
credential_path: Sign up at transcriptapi.com, copy key from dashboard; 100 free credits, then $5/month for 5,000.
breadth_note: Seven read-only endpoints: transcript, info, search, channel resolve, channel videos, playlist videos.

mcp.note: Vendor markets a YouTube MCP for ChatGPT and Claude sharing the same credit pool; MCP endpoint URL not captured.

rate_limits: 300 requests/minute per API key
notes: Small independent vendor, not Google. Base transcriptapi.com/api/v2. Depends on YouTube captions, so ToS and durability risk for production agents.

one_liner: Meeting recorder with full REST API, OAuth2, access tokens and webhooks.
auth_notes: Bearer personal or workspace access token, or OAuth2 authorization code with PKCE; Public-Api-Version header required.
credential_path: Personal tokens on Starter and above; workspace tokens need Business/Enterprise admin. Free plan has no API.
breadth_note: Recordings CRUD and upload, transcripts (json/txt/vtt/srt), AI notes, tags, sharing, users, teams, webhooks.

mcp.note: No official Grain MCP server found in developers.grain.com or the support article reviewed.

rate_limits: 300 requests/minute per token
notes: Base api.grain.com. Webhook events include recording.added, highlight.added, recording.removed. Workspace tokens expose all workspace data.
